title: MacPaw taps Liquid AI to offer on-device inference to devs building for its app store
slides: MacPaw bets on Liquid AI—will on-device inference win developers?
Developers for Setapp now get new AI tooling options.
Liquid AI's models run locally, bypassing cloud costs entirely.
This shifts app privacy, latency, and subscription pricing models.
Test your next prototype with Liquid's on-device models today.
thread_text:
1. Cloud costs are dead

Liquid AI's models run fully on-device, so developers can skip cloud fees entirely—but the real question is whether they'll trust local inference over centralized power.

2. Setapp developers get new tools

MacPaw's move means Setapp devs can now prototype with Liquid AI's on-device models, testing latency and privacy without a server bill.

3. Privacy becomes the selling point

On-device inference shifts app privacy—user data never leaves the device, which changes subscription pricing models forever.

4. Pricing models must adapt

With no cloud costs, subscription fees could drop, but developers must weigh setup complexity against savings—will users notice?

5. Test your prototype locally

Take your current app's most data-heavy feature and run it with Liquid's on-device model. Does it match cloud performance? Try it today.

instagram.caption:
Your cloud bill for AI features just got a lot smaller. 🧾

MacPaw is letting Setapp developers run Liquid AI models directly on the device—no server calls, no per-token fees. That means user data stays on the phone, and latency drops to near-zero.

For developers, the trade-off is setup complexity vs. predictable costs. Subscription prices could fall if this catches on, but only if local models match cloud performance.

If you're building an app with a heavy AI feature, test it locally today: grab Liquid's model and run your most data-hungry workflow on-device. Does it hold up? 🤔📱⚡
